topic: Constitutional Bodies: EC, UPSC, and CAG
description: Constitutional bodies in India are independent institutions established directly by the Constitution of India. The Election Commission (ECI), Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), and Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) are crucial pillars ensuring democratic elections, merit-based bureaucracy, and financial accountability.

sections.title: Election Commission of India (ECI)
sections.description: Established under Part XV of the Constitution, the ECI is a permanent and independent body responsible for ensuring free and fair elections in the country.

polity_articles.provision: Superintendence, direction, and control of elections to be vested in an Election Commission.
polity_articles.details: It conducts elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, the office of the President, and the office of the Vice-President of India.

polity_articles.provision: Elections to the House of the People and to the Legislative Assemblies of States to be on the basis of universal adult suffrage.
polity_articles.details: Ensures every citizen above a certain age has the right to vote without discrimination.

historical_events.significance: This date is now celebrated annually as 'National Voters' Day' in India.
Voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years. Consequently, the ECI was expanded to a multi-member body for the first time to handle the increased workload.

key_concepts.explanation: Currently, the ECI consists of one Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and two Election Commissioners (ECs). All three hold equal powers and receive equal salaries, similar to a Supreme Court Judge.

important_facts.fact: The tenure of the CEC and other Election Commissioners is 6 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
The CEC can only be removed from office through a process and on grounds similar to those for the removal of a Supreme Court Judge.

sections.title: Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)
sections.description: Covered under Part XIV of the Constitution, the UPSC is the central recruiting agency of India, functioning as an independent constitutional body.

polity_articles.provision: Public Service Commissions for the Union and for the States.
polity_articles.details: The Constitution also provides for a Joint State Public Service Commission (JSPSC) for two or more states, but JSPSC is a statutory body, not a constitutional one.
Mandates the UPSC to conduct examinations for appointments to the services of the Union.

key_concepts.explanation: UPSC's primary role is to ensure merit-based recruitment to the All India Services and Central Civil Services, protecting the bureaucracy from political patronage.

key_associations.extra_info: The Constitution does not specify the exact strength of the Commission; it is left to the discretion of the President (usually consists of 9 to 11 members including the Chairman).

important_facts.fact: The Chairman and members of the UPSC hold office for a term of 6 years or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
The expenses of the UPSC, including salaries, allowances, and pensions, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and are not subject to vote in Parliament.

sections.title: Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India
sections.description: Mentioned in Part V of the Constitution, the CAG is the head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar considered this office to be the most important under the Constitution.

polity_articles.details: The CAG is appointed by the President and can only be removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court.

polity_articles.provision: Duties and Powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General.
polity_articles.details: Authorizes Parliament to prescribe the duties of the CAG regarding the accounts of the Union and the States.
The reports of the CAG relating to the accounts of the Union shall be submitted to the President, who shall cause them to be laid before each House of Parliament.

key_concepts.explanation: The CAG ensures financial accountability of the executive to the legislature. They verify that funds allocated by Parliament are spent for the intended purpose and with proper authority.

important_facts.fact: The CAG holds office for a period of 6 years or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
To ensure absolute independence, the CAG is not eligible for any further employment under the Government of India or any State Government after retirement.

sections.title: Key Comparisons and Historical Firsts
sections.description: Important examination-oriented superlatives and relational facts combining these three constitutional bodies.

key_associations.extra_info: The CAG assists the PAC of the Parliament in examining audit reports. The CAG is famously known as the 'friend, philosopher, and guide' of the PAC.
Both the UPSC and the CAG submit their annual performance and audit reports respectively to the President, who then places them before the Parliament.

important_facts.fact: Sukumar Sen was the first Chief Election Commissioner of independent India.
V. Narahari Rao served as the first Comptroller and Auditor General of India (1948–1954).
Sir Ross Barker was the first Chairman of the Public Service Commission (the predecessor of UPSC) established in 1926.
